title: Contains Duplicate
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, return `true` if any value appears at least twice in the array, and return `false` if every element is distinct.

This is a warm-up problem for recognizing when a hash-based lookup structure turns an O(n^2) pairwise comparison into a single linear pass.

Think about what a set data structure naturally gives you for free, and how comparing sizes (or checking membership as you go) can answer the question without nested loops.

examples.explanation: The value 1 appears at indices 0 and 3.

editorial.approach: Walk through the array while adding each value to a hash set. Before inserting a value, check if it is already present in the set — if so, you've found a duplicate and can return true immediately. If you finish scanning without ever finding a value already in the set, all elements are distinct and you return false. An equivalent one-liner is to build a `Set` from the whole array and compare its size to the original array's length: if any duplicates existed, the set will be smaller.
